metaDesc: Schedule Twitch chat reminders with ItsBagelBot timers. Set each message, interval, activity threshold, offline behavior, fire cap and expiry.
title: Put regular reminders on a schedule.
lead: Use ItsBagelBot as your Twitch timer bot for social links, announcements and reminders. Each timer has its own message and interval. Activity thresholds, offline settings and stop conditions let you decide when that message belongs in chat.
howTitle: Schedule a message for your channel.
step1Desc: Connect your channel, open Timers and enable the module. Add a timer with the message you want the bot to post.
step2Desc: A new timer starts at ten minutes. Set its interval and the minimum recent chat activity it needs before posting.
step3Desc: Leave the timer live-only or allow offline posting. Add a per-stream fire cap or an expiry date for reminders that should end.
tblTitle: Timer settings and what chat sees.
tblNote: These rows come from the timer definition, not chat commands. The module starts disabled. A new timer is enabled, but it needs a message and the module enabled before it can post.
listTitle: A schedule that respects chat activity.
item1Desc: Every timer keeps its own interval. Use separate timers for messages that need different schedules.
item2Desc: A timer can require a minimum number of chat lines in a rolling window. When that threshold is not met, the bot skips the post and checks again on the next interval.
item3Desc: New timers have offline posting turned off. Turn it on for a message you want to allow while the channel is offline.
item4Desc: A fire cap limits repeats per stream. An expiry date stops the timer after the chosen time.
limitsNote: The runtime enforces a minimum interval of thirty seconds. A zero fire cap means unlimited repeats; an empty expiry leaves the timer without a date-based stop.
prereq1: Connect ItsBagelBot to your Twitch channel and enable Timers.
prereq2: Save a message on an enabled timer. Check its activity threshold and live or offline setting.
faqQ1: How do I make a Twitch chat timer?
faqA1: Enable Timers in the dashboard, add a message and choose an interval. Enable the individual timer and save it. The bot repeats that message when the timer’s conditions are met.
faqQ2: Why did my timer skip a message?
faqA2: Check whether the module and timer are enabled, whether the channel is live for a live-only timer, and whether recent chat has met the activity threshold. A fire cap or expiry can also stop further posts.
faqQ3: What are the defaults for a new timer?
faqA3: The interval is 600 seconds. The timer starts enabled with an empty message, a threshold of fifteen chat lines in ten minutes, offline posting off, an unlimited fire cap and no expiry date.
faqQ4: Can timers post while I am offline?
faqA4: Yes, if you turn on offline posting for that timer. New timers are live-only. Activity thresholds still apply when offline posting is allowed.
faqQ5: Can I stop a timer after a few posts?
faqA5: Yes. Set a maximum number of fires per stream, or choose an expiry date. You can also disable the individual timer.
ctaTitle: Schedule the reminders your chat needs.

message.label: Message
message.outcome: The message you save is posted when the timer fires.

intervalSeconds.label: Interval
intervalSeconds.outcome: The reminder repeats on its own interval when the other conditions are met.

enabled.label: Timer enabled
enabled.outcome: An enabled timer can post. Turning it off stops its scheduled messages.

minChatLines.label: Minimum chat lines
minChatLines.outcome: The bot waits for this much recent chat activity before posting.

chatWindowMinutes.label: Activity window
chatWindowMinutes.outcome: Only chat lines inside this rolling window count toward the activity threshold.

allowOffline.label: Allow offline
allowOffline.outcome: The message is live-only unless you allow this timer to post offline.

maxFiresPerStream.label: Maximum fires per stream
maxFiresPerStream.outcome: A positive limit stops repeats once the timer reaches its per-stream cap.

endsAt.label: Expiry
endsAt.outcome: The reminder stops after a configured expiry date.
